The bends is not something to mess with. I did years as a rescue diver and watched/witnessed some very stupid mistakes that could have cost people their lives. Tourist go to exotic locations, pay large sums of money, to scuba dive for the first time in their lives. Not realizing how serious it could be, many often plan to fly back home within a few hours of diving. “The Bends” is actually called Decompression Sickness. Decompression sickness can occur during a flight if a diver ascends to altitude too soon after diving, as the reduced pressure can cause nitrogen bubbles to form in the body. It is crucial for divers to wait at least 24 hours after diving before flying to minimize this risk. I’m amazed it doesn’t happen much more frequently.

The bends is not something to mess with. I did years as a rescue diver and watched/witnessed some very stupid mistakes that could have cost people their lives. Tourist go to exotic locations, pay large sums of money, to scuba dive for the first time in their lives. Not realizing how serious it could be, many often plan to fly back home within a few hours of diving. “The Bends” is actually called Decompression Sickness. Decompression sickness can occur during a flight if a diver ascends to altitude too soon after diving, as the reduced pressure can cause nitrogen bubbles to form in the body. It is crucial for divers to wait at least 24 hours after diving before flying to minimize this risk. I’m amazed it doesn’t happen much more frequently.
